      "title": "Negative cursor offsets are now passed to Django QuerySets",
      "body": "BasePaginator.get_result now uses cursor.offset directly when cursor.is_prev is true. Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets, but Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices. A crafted cursor such as 0:-10:1 can cause an AssertionError or database error and result in a 500 response on any endpoint using BasePaginator or DateTimePaginator."
    },

      "title": "OptimizedCursorPaginator explicitly allows invalid negative QuerySet offsets",
      "body": "When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with a negative start offset. Django ORM querysets do not support negative slicing, and the computed stop offset may also be negative or nonsensical. The comment stating that the ORM handles boundary conditions is incorrect; this will cause exceptions or undefined pagination behavior."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",
      "line": 840,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime ordering",
      "body": "OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on the ordered field value, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value. In organization_auditlogs.py it is used with order_by='-datetime'. For any non-empty result page, math.ceil(datetime) raises TypeError, and for non-zero cursors the WHERE clause would compare a datetime column to a numeric value. The optimized audit-log pagination path is therefore broken."
    },

      "file": "src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py",

      "severity": "medium",

      "title": "Unguarded access to organization_context.member may raise AttributeError",
      "body": "The code accesses organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking whether organization_context.member is None. If a request has an organization context without a member, this will raise AttributeError and return a 500 instead of denying access or falling back safely."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py",
      "line": 73,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "New optimized pagination path is untested",
      "body": "The PR adds a new optimized_pagination query-parameter branch and uses OptimizedCursorPaginator, but no tests cover this endpoint behavior or the new paginator. Given the datetime incompatibility and negative-offset handling, this is a high-risk untested code path."
    },

      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Switch from Redis sets to sorted sets is not backward compatible with in-flight data",
      "body": "Existing span-buf:s:* keys created by the previous code are Redis sets. The new code uses ZADD here, and the Lua script uses ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE, while flushing uses ZSCAN. During a rollout, pre-existing set-typed keys will cause WRONGTYPE errors, causing span buffering or flushing to fail until those keys expire. This needs a migration strategy, dual-type handling, or a new key namespace."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
      "line": 47,
      "severity": "medium",

      "body": "ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM. If the same span payload exists in both the destination and source sorted sets, for example due to duplicate delivery, retries, or overlapping buffer keys, its score becomes the sum of end_timestamp_precise values rather than the original timestamp. This corrupts eviction ordering. The union should use an explicit aggregation such as MAX or MIN."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",

      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Eviction can silently drop spans, including root spans, while preserving has-root state",
      "body": "The script evicts the lowest-scored members with ZPOPMIN when a segment exceeds 1000 spans. There is no metric or explicit signal that data was dropped. If the evicted member is the root span, the has_root_span key may still be set because is_root_span was observed, causing the segment to be flushed with root-based timing while missing its root span. This can produce incomplete or inconsistent trace segments."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
      "line": 30,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Reduced redirect-following limit may fragment deep traces",
      "body": "The redirect traversal loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000. If a trace has a redirect chain longer than 1000, new spans will stop at an intermediate redirect target and be stored under the wrong set key, fragmenting the segment. The PR provides no migration or test coverage for this behavioral change."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py",
      "line": 141,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Consumer hard-fails if end_timestamp_precise is missing",
      "body": "The consumer now reads val['end_timestamp_precise'] directly. If an incoming span message omits this field or provides null due to schema drift, older producers, or malformed data, the consumer will raise KeyError or later fail when using the value as a Redis score. This makes the consumer fragile to upstream variations."
    },

There is no coverage for segments exceeding the span cap, eviction order, root-span eviction, stale queue entries, or compatibility with old set-typed Redis keys."

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets are now passed to Django QuerySets
findings.body: BasePaginator.get_result now uses cursor.offset directly when cursor.is_prev is true. Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets, but Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices. A crafted cursor such as 0:-10:1 can cause an AssertionError or database error and result in a 500 response on any endpoint using BasePaginator or DateTimePaginator.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator explicitly allows invalid negative QuerySet offsets
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with a negative start offset. Django ORM querysets do not support negative slicing, and the computed stop offset may also be negative or nonsensical. The comment stating that the ORM handles boundary conditions is incorrect; this will cause exceptions or undefined pagination behavior.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime ordering
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on the ordered field value, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value. In organization_auditlogs.py it is used with order_by='-datetime'. For any non-empty result page, math.ceil(datetime) raises TypeError, and for non-zero cursors the WHERE clause would compare a datetime column to a numeric value. The optimized audit-log pagination path is therefore broken.

findings.title: Unguarded access to organization_context.member may raise AttributeError
findings.body: The code accesses organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking whether organization_context.member is None. If a request has an organization context without a member, this will raise AttributeError and return a 500 instead of denying access or falling back safely.

findings.title: New optimized pagination path is untested
findings.body: The PR adds a new optimized_pagination query-parameter branch and uses OptimizedCursorPaginator, but no tests cover this endpoint behavior or the new paginator. Given the datetime incompatibility and negative-offset handling, this is a high-risk untested code path.

findings.title: Switch from Redis sets to sorted sets is not backward compatible with in-flight data
findings.body: Existing span-buf:s:* keys created by the previous code are Redis sets. The new code uses ZADD here, and the Lua script uses ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE, while flushing uses ZSCAN. During a rollout, pre-existing set-typed keys will cause WRONGTYPE errors, causing span buffering or flushing to fail until those keys expire. This needs a migration strategy, dual-type handling, or a new key namespace.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE default SUM aggregation can corrupt span scores
findings.body: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM. If the same span payload exists in both the destination and source sorted sets, for example due to duplicate delivery, retries, or overlapping buffer keys, its score becomes the sum of end_timestamp_precise values rather than the original timestamp. This corrupts eviction ordering. The union should use an explicit aggregation such as MAX or MIN.

findings.title: Eviction can silently drop spans, including root spans, while preserving has-root state
findings.body: The script evicts the lowest-scored members with ZPOPMIN when a segment exceeds 1000 spans. There is no metric or explicit signal that data was dropped. If the evicted member is the root span, the has_root_span key may still be set because is_root_span was observed, causing the segment to be flushed with root-based timing while missing its root span. This can produce incomplete or inconsistent trace segments.

findings.title: Reduced redirect-following limit may fragment deep traces
findings.body: The redirect traversal loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000. If a trace has a redirect chain longer than 1000, new spans will stop at an intermediate redirect target and be stored under the wrong set key, fragmenting the segment. The PR provides no migration or test coverage for this behavioral change.

findings.title: Consumer hard-fails if end_timestamp_precise is missing
findings.body: The consumer now reads val['end_timestamp_precise'] directly. If an incoming span message omits this field or provides null due to schema drift, older producers, or malformed data, the consumer will raise KeyError or later fail when using the value as a Redis score. This makes the consumer fragile to upstream variations.

findings.title: No tests cover the new eviction behavior or sorted-set migration
findings.body: The core behavioral changes in this PR are the switch from sets to sorted sets and eviction of segments above 1000 spans, but the tests only add end_timestamp_precise values. There is no coverage for segments exceeding the span cap, eviction order, root-span eviction, stale queue entries, or compatibility with old set-typed Redis keys.
